pelage_geometry_and_topology.patch_morphology: Irregular polygonal dark regions with relatively smooth edge gradients. Patches on the lateral flank exhibit larger spatial area and more elongated geometries compared to the smaller, more compact patches observed on the cervical region.
pelage_geometry_and_topology.corridor_network: A continuous network of light pelage pathways forming a topological graph. Junction nodes primarily consist of three-way and four-way intersections. The pixel thickness of these pathways is consistent across the visible torso, maintaining clear separation between dark patches.

dorsal_ridge_profile.edge_serration: A low-amplitude, high-frequency jagged silhouette of dark hair along the dorsal ridge, extending from the upper neck through the shoulder. The mane is clearly defined as a dark boundary against the background.

other_distinctive_markers: Two dark-colored avian subjects (likely Buphagus species) are perched on the dorsal ridge and the posterior flank area, causing localized occlusions of the pelage pattern.
